lines: The kettle hums a little song,
the window blushes pink.
You don't have to rush along,
there's time to breathe and think.
A flower doesn't ask the rain
if it deserves the sky.
It simply opens up again
and lets the storm go by.
Tonight the moon is only half,
and still she lights the lane.
You needn't be whole to shine,
or perfect to remain.
Hold the cup with both your hands,
let warm steam find your face.
The world can wait a minute more.
This moment is a resting place.
The rain is writing on the glass
in letters soft and slow:
it's okay to stay inside today,
it's okay to not yet know.
Some seeds sleep through winter long
beneath the frozen ground.
They are not late, they are not lost,
they're growing without sound.
Good morning, little tired heart,
you made it through the night.
We'll take the day one step at a time
and look for bits of light.
The sky is never rushed to turn
from quiet gray to gold.
So take your time, and let yourself
be softly, warmly held.
A daisy growing through the crack
where no one planned a flower:
proof that small and stubborn things
have their own kind of power.
Put down the list, put down the weight,
just for a breath or two.
The stars came out without a plan,
and still they shine for you.
The puddles hold a piece of sky
on every little street.
Even on the grayest days
there's blue beneath your feet.
You watered all the plants today
and quite forgot your own.
Here's a glass of water, friend.
You're something that has grown.
The moon won't mind if you're awake,
she's used to keeping late.
Lie still and listen to the quiet.
Sleep will come. It's safe to wait.
Morning spills across the floor
like honey, slow and sweet.
Stretch a little, sigh a little,
there's no one you must beat.
Petals fall, and that's alright,
the tree is not undone.
It's only making room again
for something new to come.
One cup of tea, one open window,
one bird upon the wire.
Not every day needs something big.
Small things can light the fire.
Let the rain do all the work
of washing the day clean.
You only have to listen,
curled up and warm, unseen.
If today was heavy,
set it down by the door.
You carried it so far already.
You don't need to carry more.
The sunflowers turn to find the light
a little every hour.
You're turning too, though slow and small,
and one day you will flower.
Good night to the teacup,
good night to the rain,
good night to the worries
that came and went again.
Good night to the moon
keeping watch while you sleep.
Whatever tomorrow asks,
tonight is yours to keep.
